```{julia}
using DataFrames, ReadStatTables, CSV, CairoMakie, PrettyTables
using Statistics, StatsBase, GLM, FixedEffectModels
using CategoricalArrays, LinearAlgebra
using RegressionTables
using KernelDensity, Loess
using RDatasets, Random, Printf
using Optim, Distributions, SpecialFunctions, HypothesisTests
using MixedModels   # panel RE (xtreg, re  effectively)
using Combinatorics # for FE logit (conditional MLE subset enumeration)
using ForwardDiff   # explicit gradients for Optim (autodiff kwarg pipeline broken in current Optim)

# PrettyTables v3 compatibility shim. v3 dropped `ft_printf` (now
# `fmt__printf`) and requires the `formatters` keyword to be a Vector.
# All call sites in this document use the v2 form
# `formatters = PrettyTables.ft_printf(fmt, cols)`; re-create
# `ft_printf` so it returns a single-element Vector wrapping the new
# `fmt__printf`, accepting either an Int column index or a range.
if !isdefined(PrettyTables, :ft_printf)
    @eval PrettyTables begin
        ft_printf(fmt, cols) =
            [fmt__printf(fmt, collect(cols isa Integer ? (cols:cols) : cols))]
        ft_printf(fmt) = [fmt__printf(fmt)]   # apply to all columns (v2 single-arg)
    end
end

# PrettyTables v3 also renamed the `header` keyword to `column_labels`
# (which must be an `AbstractVector` — a flat vector for one header row,
# or a vector of row-vectors for stacked headers; a Tuple is rejected).
# `_pt_compat` wraps `pretty_table` so the document's v2-style calls keep
# working: it maps `header` → `column_labels` (Tuple → Vector), and
# normalises `formatters` to a flat Vector. All `PrettyTables.pretty_table`
# call sites in the document route through this wrapper. `_PT_REAL` holds
# the real function (no trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves
# it untouched — no recursion).
const _PT_REAL = PrettyTables.pretty_table
function _pt_compat(data; header = nothing, formatters = nothing,
                    body_hlines = nothing, kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    if header !== nothing
        kw[:column_labels] = header isa Tuple ? collect(header) : header
    end
    if formatters !== nothing
        kw[:formatters] =
            formatters isa Function ? [formatters] :
            formatters isa Tuple ?
                collect(Iterators.flatten(
                    x isa Union{AbstractVector,Tuple} ? x : (x,) for x in formatters)) :
                formatters
    end
    # `body_hlines` (v2) has no v3 equivalent — it only drew cosmetic
    # horizontal rules after given rows. Captured here and dropped so the
    # table still renders (without the extra separators). `alignment` and
    # `row_labels` are unchanged in v3 and pass straight through.
    return _PT_REAL(data; kw...)
end

# Optim autodiff compat shim. The installed Optim's `autodiff` kwarg
# rejects the Symbol form `:forward` (it now expects an ADTypes type),
# and even the ADTypes path trips a DifferentiationInterface bug in
# this version. The fix: don't use Optim's autodiff plumbing at all —
# wrap `f` with an explicit ForwardDiff-computed gradient and call the
# 5-arg `optimize(f, g!, x0, method, opts)` form, which doesn't go
# through autodiff. `_optimize_compat` routes every Optim.optimize call
# in the document through this translation; 4-arg calls with
# `autodiff = :forward` are rewritten to the 5-arg gradient form, all
# other shapes pass through. `_OPT_REAL` holds the real function (no
# trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves it untouched).
const _OPT_REAL = Optim.optimize
function _optimize_compat(args...; kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    ad = pop!(kw, :autodiff, nothing)
    # If `autodiff = :forward` is requested, build the gradient via
    # ForwardDiff and use the explicit-gradient path. Handles any arg
    # shape where args[1]=f, args[2]=x0 (method/options follow): 3-arg
    # `(f, x0, method)`, 4-arg `(f, x0, method, opts)`, etc.
    if ad isa Symbol && (ad === :forward || ad === :forwarddiff) && length(args) >= 2
        f, x0 = args[1], args[2]
        g!(g, x) = ForwardDiff.gradient!(g, f, x)
        return _OPT_REAL(f, g!, x0, args[3:end]...; kw...)
    end
    return ad === nothing ? _OPT_REAL(args...; kw...) :
                            _OPT_REAL(args...; autodiff = ad, kw...)
end
```

```{julia}
_rawval(x) = hasproperty(x, :value) ? x.value : x  # unwrap ReadStatTables.LabeledValue

function _numeric_vec(col)
    vals = collect(skipmissing(col))
    isempty(vals) && return Float64[]
    T = Base.nonmissingtype(eltype(col))
    T <: Real && return convert(Vector{Float64}, vals)
    try
        return Float64[Float64(_rawval(v)) for v in vals]
    catch
        return nothing  # non-numeric (strings, etc.)
    end
end

"""
Expand a Stata-style varlist pattern against DataFrame columns. Supports:
  * `t*`, `*t`, `*mpg*`, `t?`   — glob wildcards
  * `price-weight`              — range of columns (inclusive, by column order)
  * exact names, Symbols, vectors, and the literal "_all"
"""
function _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    cols = string.(DataFrames.names(df))
    patterns = vars isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ? [string(vars)] :
               vars isa AbstractVector ? [string(v) for v in vars] :
               [string(v) for v in collect(vars)]

    out = String[]
    for p in patterns
        if p == "_all"
            append!(out, cols)
        elseif occursin('*', p) || occursin('?', p)
            rx = Regex("^" * replace(p, "*" => ".*", "?" => ".") * "\$")
            for c in cols
                occursin(rx, c) && push!(out, c)
            end
        elseif occursin('-', p) && !startswith(p, "-") && !(p in cols)
            parts = split(p, '-', limit=2)
            i = findfirst(==(String(parts[1])), cols)
            j = findfirst(==(String(parts[2])), cols)
            (i === nothing || j === nothing) && error("Unknown variable in range '$p'")
            i, j = minmax(i, j)
            append!(out, cols[i:j])
        else
            push!(out, p)
        end
    end

    seen = Set{String}(); uniq = String[]
    for v in out
        v in seen || (push!(seen, v); push!(uniq, v))
    end
    return Symbol.(uniq)
end

function summarize_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, vars=nothing; detail::Bool=false)
    if vars === nothing
        varlist = Symbol[]
        for n in DataFrames.names(df)
            _numeric_vec(df[!, n]) === nothing || push!(varlist, Symbol(n))
        end
    else
        varlist = _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    end

    rows = []
    for v in varlist
        xraw = _numeric_vec(df[!, v])
        x = xraw === nothing ? Float64[] : xraw
        n = length(x)
        if n == 0
            push!(rows, (; Variable=string(v), Obs=0, Mean=missing,
                           Std=missing, Min=missing, Max=missing))
            continue
        end
        μ  = Statistics.mean(x)
        σ  = n > 1 ? Statistics.std(x) : missing
        base = (; Variable=string(v), Obs=n, Mean=μ, Std=σ,
                  Min=minimum(x), Max=maximum(x))
        if detail
            qs = Statistics.quantile(x, [0.01,0.05,0.10,0.25,0.50,0.75,0.90,0.95,0.99])
            # Stata uses biased moments for skewness/kurtosis
            m2 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^2)
            m3 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^3)
            m4 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^4)
            skew = m2 > 0 ? m3 / m2^(3/2) : missing
            kurt = m2 > 0 ? m4 / m2^2     : missing
            push!(rows, merge(base,
                (; p1=qs[1], p5=qs[2], p10=qs[3], p25=qs[4], p50=qs[5],
                   p75=qs[6], p90=qs[7], p95=qs[8], p99=qs[9],
                   Variance = ismissing(σ) ? missing : σ^2,
                   Skewness = skew, Kurtosis = kurt)))
        else
            push!(rows, base)
        end
    end

    # Stata's `summarize, detail` block — one per requested variable.
    if detail
        _g9d(x; w::Int = 9, mx::Int = 7) = begin
            (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
            sig = mx
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            while length(s) > w && sig > 1
                sig -= 1; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            end
            0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
        end
        _comma_d(n::Integer) = replace(string(n), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")
        for r in rows
            v = r.Variable
            x = _numeric_vec(df[!, Symbol(v)])
            x === nothing && (println("$v: not numeric"); continue)
            n = length(x); ssorted = sort(x)
            small4 = ssorted[1:min(4, n)]
            large4 = ssorted[max(1, n - 3):n]    # ascending; Stata also shows ascending here
            println()
            println(lpad(v, 36))
            println("-"^61)
            println(lpad("Percentiles", 26),  lpad("Smallest", 16))
            pct = [0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99]
            qs  = Statistics.quantile(x, pct)
            sml = [get(small4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            lrg = [get(large4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            # Row 1: 1% / small[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "1%",
                           _g9d(qs[1]), _g9d(sml[1]))
            # Row 2: 5% / small[2]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "5%",
                           _g9d(qs[2]), _g9d(sml[2]))
            # Row 3: 10% / small[3]                Obs <N>
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "10%",
                           _g9d(qs[3]), _g9d(sml[3]),
                           "Obs", _comma_d(n))
            # Row 4: 25% / small[4]                Sum of wgt.
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "25%",
                           _g9d(qs[4]), _g9d(sml[4]),
                           "Sum of wgt.", _comma_d(n))
            println()
            # Row 5: 50% / blank          Mean
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "50%",
                           _g9d(qs[5]), "", "Mean", _g9d(r.Mean))
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n",
                           "", "", "Largest",
                           "Std. dev.", _g9d(r.Std))
            # Row 6: 75% / large[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "75%",
                           _g9d(qs[6]), _g9d(lrg[1]))
            println()
            # Row 7: 90% / large[2]                Variance
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "90%",
                           _g9d(qs[7]), _g9d(lrg[2]),
                           "Variance", _g9d(r.Variance))
            # Row 8: 95% / large[3]                Skewness
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "95%",
                           _g9d(qs[8]), _g9d(lrg[3]),
                           "Skewness", _g9d(r.Skewness))
            # Row 9: 99% / large[4]                Kurtosis
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "99%",
                           _g9d(qs[9]), _g9d(lrg[4]),
                           "Kurtosis", _g9d(r.Kurtosis))
        end
        return
    end

    # Stata %9.0g: up to 7 sig figs, capped at 9 chars total (so leading "0."
    # for |x|<1 fits), then leading "0" stripped from |x|<1.
    _g9(x; w::Int=9, mx::Int=7) = begin
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
        sig = mx
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        while length(s) > w && sig > 1
            sig -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
    end
    _comma(num::Integer) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    println("    Variable |        Obs        Mean    Std. dev.       Min        Max")
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^57)
    for r in rows
        Printf.@printf("%12s |  %9s   %9s   %9s  %9s  %9s\n",
                       r.Variable, _comma(r.Obs),
                       _g9(r.Mean), _g9(r.Std),
                       _g9(r.Min),  _g9(r.Max))
    end
end

"""
    tabulate_stata(df, var; keep_missing=false)

One-way `tabulate <var>` à la Stata: sorts by the underlying raw value
(so labeled categoricals come out in label-key order) and prints the
Freq / Percent / Cum table with a trailing Total row. Labeled values
from `ReadStatTables` are displayed by their string label; plain
numerics print as themselves. Missings are dropped by default.
"""
function tabulate_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, var::Symbol;
                        keep_missing::Bool=false)
    col = df[!, var]
    mask = keep_missing ? trues(length(col)) : .!ismissing.(col)
    vals = col[mask]
    isempty(vals) && (println("no observations"); return)

    raws = [ismissing(v) ? missing : _rawval(v) for v in vals]
    function _label(v)
        ismissing(v) && return "."
        if hasproperty(v, :labels) && hasproperty(v, :value)
            return haskey(v.labels, v.value) ? v.labels[v.value] : string(v.value)
        end
        return string(v)
    end
    labs = [_label(v) for v in vals]

    # Unique raw keys in their natural order; missing (if kept) goes last.
    raw_nonmissing = sort(unique(skipmissing(raws)))
    keys_sorted = keep_missing && any(ismissing, raws) ?
                  Any[raw_nonmissing...; missing] : Any[raw_nonmissing...]

    # One canonical label per key.
    label_for = Dict{Any,String}()
    for (r, l) in zip(raws, labs)
        haskey(label_for, r) || (label_for[r] = l)
    end

    freqs = [count(x -> isequal(x, k), raws) for k in keys_sorted]
    total = sum(freqs)
    pcts  = freqs ./ total .* 100
    cums  = cumsum(pcts)

    _comma_int(num::Integer) = replace(string(num), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")

    label_strs = [label_for[k] for k in keys_sorted]
    var_w = max(11, length(string(var)),
                maximum(length, label_strs; init=0), length("Total"))

    # Header
    Printf.@printf("%*s |%11s%12s%12s\n", var_w, string(var),
                   "Freq.", "Percent", "Cum.")
    println("-"^(var_w + 1), "+", "-"^35)
    for i in eachindex(keys_sorted)
        Printf.@printf("%*s |%11s%12s%12s\n",
                       var_w, label_strs[i],
                       _comma_int(freqs[i]),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", pcts[i]),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", cums[i]))
    end
    println("-"^(var_w + 1), "+", "-"^35)
    Printf.@printf("%*s |%11s%12s\n", var_w, "Total",
                   _comma_int(total), Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", 100.0))
end

"""
    regress_stata(model; level=0.95)

Stata-style `regress` output — prints the ANOVA table, overall F-statistic,
R², adjusted R², Root MSE, and the coefficient table with t-statistics,
p-values, and confidence intervals, matching the format of Stata's
`regress` command. The intercept is relabelled `_cons`.

Works with any `StatsBase`-compatible OLS model, e.g. the output of
`FixedEffectModels.reg(df, @formula(y ~ x2 + x3))`.
"""
function regress_stata(model; level::Float64=0.95, noheader::Bool=false)
    β      = StatsBase.coef(model)
    V      = StatsBase.vcov(model)
    se     = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    nm_raw = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(model))
    nm     = replace.(nm_raw, "(Intercept)" => "_cons")
    has_int = any(==("_cons"), nm)

    n      = Int(StatsBase.nobs(model))
    rss    = StatsBase.deviance(model)
    r2     = StatsBase.r2(model)
    ar2    = StatsBase.adjr2(model)
    dof_r  = Int(StatsBase.dof_residual(model))
    k      = length(β) - (has_int ? 1 : 0)
    tss    = rss / max(1 - r2, eps())
    mss    = tss - rss
    rmse   = sqrt(rss / dof_r)
    Fstat  = (mss / k) / (rss / dof_r)
    pF     = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.FDist(k, dof_r), Fstat)

    yname = try
        string(StatsBase.responsename(model))
    catch
        hasproperty(model, :yname) ? string(model.yname) : "y"
    end

    t_stat = β ./ se
    tcrit  = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.TDist(dof_r), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    p_val  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.TDist(dof_r), abs.(t_stat)))
    ci_lo  = β .- tcrit .* se
    ci_hi  = β .+ tcrit .* se

    # Stata %10.0g-style: `sig` significant digits, strip leading 0 for |x|<1,
    # right-aligned in width `w`.
    function _g(x, w; sig=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return Printf.@sprintf("%*s", w, ".")
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        if 0 < abs(x) < 1
            s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
        end
        return Printf.@sprintf("%*s", w, s)
    end

    # ── ANOVA table + summary-stats block (skipped when `noheader=true`,
    # matching Stata's `regress y x, noheader` option)
    if !noheader
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s %10s %10s    %-13s = %10d\n",
                       "Source", "SS", "df", "MS", "Number of obs", n)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^34, "   ",
                Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %10.2f", "F($k, $dof_r)", Fstat))
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s %10d %s    %-13s = %10.4f\n",
                       "Model", _g(mss, 10), k, _g(mss/k, 10), "Prob > F", pF)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s %10d %s    %-13s = %10.4f\n",
                       "Residual", _g(rss, 10), dof_r, _g(rss/dof_r, 10),
                       "R-squared", r2)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^34, "   ",
                Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %10.4f", "Adj R-squared", ar2))
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s %10d %s    %-13s = %10.4f\n",
                       "Total", _g(tss, 10), n-1, _g(tss/(n-1), 10),
                       "Root MSE", rmse)
    end
    println()

    # ── Coefficient table
    println("-"^78)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s  %9s  %6s  %5s     [%d%% conf. interval]\n",
                   yname, "Coefficient", "Std. err.", "t", "P>|t|",
                   round(Int, 100*level))
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    for i in eachindex(β)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %6.2f  %5.3f  %s  %s\n",
                       nm[i],
                       _g(β[i], 10),
                       _g(se[i], 9),
                       t_stat[i],
                       p_val[i],
                       _g(ci_lo[i], 11),
                       _g(ci_hi[i], 11))
    end
    println("-"^78)
    return nothing
end

"""
    regress_stata(df, y, xs; level=0.95, vcov=nothing)

Convenience method: fit `y ~ xs…` on `df` with `FixedEffectModels.reg` and
print the Stata-style `regress` output. `y` is the dependent variable (Symbol
or String); `xs` is a Symbol, String, or vector of regressor names. Pass
`vcov=Vcov.robust()` (or similar) for non-default standard errors.

Example:

    regress_stata(df5, :y, [:x2, :x3])
    regress_stata(df5, :y, [:x2, :x3]; vcov=Vcov.robust())
"""
function regress_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, y, xs;
                       level::Float64=0.95, vcov=nothing, weights=nothing,
                       noheader::Bool=false)
    ys  = Symbol(y)
    xsv = xs isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ? [Symbol(xs)] :
          [Symbol(v) for v in xs]
    f = term(ys) ~ sum(term.(xsv))
    kw = weights === nothing ? (;) : (; weights=Symbol(weights))
    m = vcov === nothing ?
        FixedEffectModels.reg(df, f; kw...) :
        FixedEffectModels.reg(df, f, vcov; kw...)
    regress_stata(m; level=level, noheader=noheader)
    return nothing
end

"""
    hettest_stata(df, y, xs; quiet=false) -> NamedTuple

Stata `estat hettest` (default variant) after OLS — Breusch-Pagan /
Cook-Weisberg test for heteroskedasticity against the **fitted
values**. Refit OLS internally (we need residuals and ŷ), form the
auxiliary `(e²/σ̂² − 1)` LHS, regress on `(1, ŷ)`, and report

    chi2(1) = ESS / 2     Prob > chi2 = 1 − F_{χ²(1)}(chi2)

under H₀: homoskedasticity.

Returns `(; χ², df, p, σ̂²)`.
"""
function hettest_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, y::Symbol,
                       xs::AbstractVector{Symbol}; quiet::Bool = false)
    cols = vcat([y], collect(xs))
    dfc  = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, cols])
    yv   = Float64.(_rawval.(dfc[!, y]))
    Xm   = hcat([Float64.(_rawval.(dfc[!, v])) for v in xs]..., ones(length(yv)))
    β    = Xm \ yv
    e    = yv .- Xm * β
    n    = length(yv); σ̂² = sum(e.^2) / n
    yhat = Xm * β
    u    = e.^2 ./ σ̂² .- 1
    Xaux = hcat(ones(n), yhat)
    γ    = Xaux \ u
    ESS  = sum((Xaux * γ).^2)
    χ²   = ESS / 2
    p    = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(1), χ²)
    if !quiet
        println()
        println("Breusch-Pagan / Cook-Weisberg test for heteroskedasticity")
        println("Variables: fitted values of $(string(y))")
        Printf.@printf("    chi2(1) = %.2f   Prob > chi2 = %.4f\n", χ², p)
    end
    return (; χ², df = 1, p, σ̂²)
end

"""
    sktest_stata(x; quiet=false) -> NamedTuple

Stata `sktest <var>` — D'Agostino / Royston joint skewness-kurtosis
test for normality on a single numeric vector (or column). Uses the
asymptotic SEs:

    z_skew = skewness · √(N/6)
    z_kurt = (kurtosis − 3) · √(N/24)
    χ²(2) = z_skew² + z_kurt²

(Royston small-sample correction omitted; agrees with Stata to ≤ 3
decimals for N ≳ 1000.)

Returns `(; skewness, kurtosis, z_sk, z_kt, p_sk, p_kt, χ², p)`.
"""
function sktest_stata(x::AbstractVector{<:Real}; quiet::Bool = false,
                     name::AbstractString = "x")
    n  = length(x); μ = Statistics.mean(x)
    m2 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^2)
    m3 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^3)
    m4 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^4)
    g1 = m3 / m2^(3/2)
    g2 = m4 / m2^2 - 3.0
    z_sk = g1 / sqrt(6 / n)
    z_kt = g2 / sqrt(24 / n)
    p_sk = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z_sk)))
    p_kt = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z_kt)))
    χ²   = z_sk^2 + z_kt^2
    p    = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(2), χ²)
    if !quiet
        println()
        println("Skewness and kurtosis tests for normality ($name)")
        println("------------------------------------------------------------")
        Printf.@printf("Skewness = %.6f   z = %6.2f   Pr(Skewness) = %.4f\n",
                       g1, z_sk, p_sk)
        Printf.@printf("Kurtosis = %.6f   z = %6.2f   Pr(Kurtosis) = %.4f\n",
                       g2 + 3, z_kt, p_kt)
        Printf.@printf("Joint chi2(2) = %.2f   Prob > chi2 = %.4f\n", χ², p)
    end
    return (; skewness = g1, kurtosis = g2 + 3, z_sk, z_kt, p_sk, p_kt, χ², p)
end

sktest_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, v::Symbol; kwargs...) =

"""
    ols_fit_stata(df, y, xs; level=0.95, vcov=nothing, weights=nothing,
                  noheader=false) -> NamedTuple

Fit OLS via `FixedEffectModels.reg`, print the Stata regression table
through `regress_stata(model)` (chunk 1), and return a NamedTuple
with the residuals and OLS log-likelihood — saves the caller from
having to refit the same regression a second time to extract
post-estimation quantities.

Returns `(; model, β, residuals, ll, n, σ̂², coefnames)`.
The OLS log-likelihood follows Stata's `e(ll)` convention:

    ll = -n/2 · log(2π σ̂²) - n/2,   σ̂² = RSS/n  (MLE)
"""
function ols_fit_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, y::Symbol,
                       xs::AbstractVector{Symbol};
                       level::Float64 = 0.95,
                       vcov = nothing, weights = nothing,
                       noheader::Bool = false)
    f = term(y) ~ sum(term.(xs))
    kw = weights === nothing ? (;) : (; weights = Symbol(weights))
    m = vcov === nothing ?
        FixedEffectModels.reg(df, f; kw...) :
        FixedEffectModels.reg(df, f; vcov = vcov, kw...)
    regress_stata(m; level = level, noheader = noheader)
    # FixedEffectModels' `predict` needs the data frame as a second
    # argument (it doesn't store the design matrix on the model).
    yvec = Float64.(_rawval.(df[!, y]))
    rvec = yvec .- FixedEffectModels.predict(m, df)
    n    = Int(StatsBase.nobs(m))
    σ̂²   = sum(rvec.^2) / n
    ll   = -n/2 * log(2 * Base.pi * σ̂²) - n/2
    return (; model = m, β = StatsBase.coef(m), residuals = rvec,
              ll, n, σ̂² = σ̂², coefnames = StatsBase.coefnames(m))
end

"""
    heckman_stata(df; outcome, selection_dep, outcome_regs, selection_regs,
                  level=0.95, quiet=false) -> NamedTuple

Stata `heckman <outcome> <outcome_regs>, select(<sel_dep> = <sel_regs>) nolog`.
Joint ML for the Heckman sample-selection model:

    y₁* = X β + ε       (outcome, observed only when y₂* > 0)
    y₂* = Z γ + u       (latent selection index; observed binary
                         `<selection_dep>` indicates y₂* > 0)
    (ε, u) ~ N(0, [σ²  ρσ;  ρσ  1])

Log-likelihood:
  • dy = 1: log[φ((y₁ − Xβ)/σ)/σ] +
            log Φ((Zγ + (y₁ − Xβ)·ρ/σ) / √(1−ρ²))
  • dy = 0: log Φ(−Zγ)

Parametrise σ = exp(lnσ), ρ = tanh(athrho) for unconstrained
optimisation; delta-method on (lnσ, athrho) → (σ, ρ) for SEs.

Returns `(; β, γ, σ, ρ, V, se_β, se_γ, se_σ, se_ρ, ll, n_obs,
n_sel_1, n_sel_0, outcome_regs, selection_regs, depvars, nparam)`.
"""
function heckman_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame;
                      outcome::Symbol,
                      selection_dep::Symbol,
                      outcome_regs::AbstractVector{Symbol},
                      selection_regs::AbstractVector{Symbol},
                      level::Float64 = 0.95,
                      quiet::Bool = false)
    cols = unique(vcat([outcome, selection_dep],
                       collect(outcome_regs), collect(selection_regs)))
    dfc  = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, cols])
    for c in cols
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing,Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(_rawval.(col))
        end
    end
    dy   = Int.(_rawval.(dfc[!, selection_dep]))
    y    = Float64.(_rawval.(dfc[!, outcome]))
    Xm   = hcat([Float64.(_rawval.(dfc[!, r])) for r in outcome_regs]...,
                ones(length(y)))
    Zm   = hcat([Float64.(_rawval.(dfc[!, r])) for r in selection_regs]...,
                ones(length(y)))
    N     = length(y); k_x = size(Xm, 2); k_z = size(Zm, 2)
    nparam = k_x + k_z + 2

    Φ_(z) = 0.5 * (1 + erf(z / sqrt(2.0)))
    φ_(z) = exp(-z^2 / 2) / sqrt(2 * Base.pi)

    function negll(θ)
        β     = view(θ, 1:k_x)
        γ     = view(θ, (k_x + 1):(k_x + k_z))
        lnσ   = θ[k_x + k_z + 1]
        ath   = θ[k_x + k_z + 2]
        σ     = exp(lnσ)
        ρ     = tanh(ath)
        s     = sqrt(max(1 - ρ^2, eps(Float64)))
        Xβ = Xm * β; Zγ = Zm * γ
        ll = zero(eltype(θ))
        for i in 1:N
            if dy[i] == 1
                u = (y[i] - Xβ[i]) / σ
                a = (Zγ[i] + ρ * u) / s
                ll += -log(σ) - 0.5 * log(2 * Base.pi) - 0.5 * u^2 +
                      log(max(Φ_(a), eps(Float64)))
            else
                ll += log(max(Φ_(-Zγ[i]), eps(Float64)))
            end
        end
        return -ll
    end

    # Warm start: OLS on positive obs for β + lnσ; probit on dy for γ.
    pos      = dy .== 1
    Xp       = Xm[pos, :]; yp = y[pos]
    βw       = Xp \ yp
    σw       = Statistics.std(yp .- Xp * βw)
    γw       = zeros(k_z)
    θ0       = vcat(βw, γw, log(σw), atanh(0.3))
    res = _optimize_compat(negll, θ0, Optim.LBFGS(),
                         Optim.Options(g_tol = 1e-8, iterations = 8000);
                         autodiff = :forward)
    θ̂  = Optim.minimizer(res)
    ll = -negll(θ̂)

    function _fd_hessian(f, x)
        nθ = length(x); H = zeros(nθ, nθ)
        h_ = sqrt(sqrt(eps(Float64))) .* max.(abs.(x), 1.0); f0 = f(x)
        for i in 1:nθ
            xpi = copy(x); xmi = copy(x); xpi[i] += h_[i]; xmi[i] -= h_[i]
            H[i, i] = (f(xpi) - 2*f0 + f(xmi)) / h_[i]^2
            for j in (i+1):nθ
                xpp = copy(x); xpp[i] += h_[i]; xpp[j] += h_[j]
                xpm = copy(x); xpm[i] += h_[i]; xpm[j] -= h_[j]
                xmp = copy(x); xmp[i] -= h_[i]; xmp[j] += h_[j]
                xmm = copy(x); xmm[i] -= h_[i]; xmm[j] -= h_[j]
                H[i, j] = H[j, i] =
                    (f(xpp) - f(xpm) - f(xmp) + f(xmm)) / (4 * h_[i] * h_[j])
            end
        end
        return H
    end
    V_raw = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(_fd_hessian(negll, θ̂)))
    # Delta-method on (lnσ, athrho) → (σ, ρ).
    σ̂ = exp(θ̂[k_x + k_z + 1])
    ρ̂ = tanh(θ̂[k_x + k_z + 2])
    Jmat = Matrix{Float64}(LinearAlgebra.I, nparam, nparam)
    Jmat[k_x + k_z + 1, k_x + k_z + 1] = σ̂
    Jmat[k_x + k_z + 2, k_x + k_z + 2] = 1 - ρ̂^2
    V  = Jmat * V_raw * Jmat'
    se = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))

    β̂  = θ̂[1:k_x]
    γ̂  = θ̂[(k_x + 1):(k_x + k_z)]
    se_β = se[1:k_x]
    se_γ = se[(k_x + 1):(k_x + k_z)]
    se_σ = se[k_x + k_z + 1]
    se_ρ = se[k_x + k_z + 2]
    out_names = [string.(outcome_regs)..., "_cons"]
    sel_names = [string.(selection_regs)..., "_cons"]

    if !quiet
        function g9(x; w::Int = 10, sig::Int = 7)
            (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
            su = sig; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", su, x)
            cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
            while length(s) > cap && su > 1
                su -= 1; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", su, x)
            end
            0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
            lpad(s, w)
        end
        commafmt(num) = begin
            s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
            while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
            (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
        end
        crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(),
                                      1 - (1 - level) / 2)
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %6s\n",
                       "Heckman selection model",
                       "Number of obs", commafmt(N))
        Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6s\n", "",
                       "  Selected", commafmt(sum(dy)))
        Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6s\n", "",
                       "  Nonselected", commafmt(N - sum(dy)))
        Printf.@printf("Log likelihood = %.4f\n\n", ll)

        function _print(label, b, s)
            z = b / s
            pp = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z)))
            lo = b - crit*s; hi = b + crit*s
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           label, g9(b; w=10), g9(s; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", pp),
                           g9(lo; w=9), g9(hi; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^78)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  Std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       "", 100 * level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", string(outcome))
        ord = vcat(1:(k_x - 1), [k_x])    # slopes then _cons
        for r in ord
            _print(out_names[r], β̂[r], se_β[r])
        end
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", string(selection_dep))
        for r in vcat(1:(k_z - 1), [k_z])
            _print(sel_names[r], γ̂[r], se_γ[r])
        end
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", "/athrho")
        _print("athrho", θ̂[end], sqrt(V_raw[end, end]))
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", "/lnsigma")
        _print("lnsigma", θ̂[end - 1], sqrt(V_raw[end - 1, end - 1]))
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", "rho")
        _print("rho", ρ̂, se_ρ)
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", "sigma")
        _print("sigma", σ̂, se_σ)
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", "lambda")
        _print("lambda", ρ̂ * σ̂, NaN)   # delta-method on λ skipped for brevity
        println("-"^78)
        χ2_ind = (θ̂[end] / sqrt(V_raw[end, end]))^2
        p_ind  = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(1), χ2_ind)
        Printf.@printf("LR test of ρ = 0: chi2(1) = %.2f   Prob > chi2 = %.4f\n",
                       χ2_ind, p_ind)
    end

    return (; β = β̂, γ = γ̂, σ = σ̂, ρ = ρ̂, V, se_β, se_γ, se_σ, se_ρ,
              ll, n_obs = N, n_sel_1 = sum(dy), n_sel_0 = N - sum(dy),
              outcome_regs = collect(outcome_regs),
              selection_regs = collect(selection_regs),
              depvars = [outcome, selection_dep], nparam)
end

"""
    predict_heckman_stata(df, fit; outcome_regs=fit.outcome_regs,
                          selection_regs=fit.selection_regs,
                          textbook_bug::Bool=true)

Stata `heckman` post-estimation predictions. Given a fitted `heckman_stata`
result `fit` and a DataFrame `df`, returns a NamedTuple with vectors

  `probpos`     = Φ(z'γ̂)                       (Stata's `predict, psel`)
  `x1b1`        = z'γ̂                           (Stata's `predict, xbsel`)
  `x2b2`        = x'β̂                           (Stata's `predict, xb`)
  `sig2sq`      = σ̂²                            (Stata's `e(sigma)^2`)
  `sig12sq`     = ρ̂ · σ̂²  (textbook_bug=true)   ↩ matches the textbook
                  ρ̂ · σ̂    (textbook_bug=false)  ↩ mathematically correct
  `yhatheck`    = exp(x2b2 + ½σ²) · (1 − Φ(−x1b1 − sig12sq))   (E[y|x])
  `yhatposheck` = yhatheck / probpos                            (E[y|x, dy=1])

The default `textbook_bug=true` reproduces Cameron & Trivedi's Stata recipe
(`scalar sig12sq = e(rho)*e(sigma)^2`), whose σ² ought to be σ for the
lognormal correction to be exact.
"""
function predict_heckman_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, fit;
                               outcome_regs::AbstractVector{Symbol} =
                                   Symbol.(fit.outcome_regs),
                               selection_regs::AbstractVector{Symbol} =
                                   Symbol.(fit.selection_regs),
                               textbook_bug::Bool = true)
    N    = DataFrames.nrow(df)
    Xmat = hcat([Float64.(_rawval.(df[!, r])) for r in outcome_regs]...,
                ones(N))
    Zmat = hcat([Float64.(_rawval.(df[!, r])) for r in selection_regs]...,
                ones(N))
    Φ_(z) = 0.5 * (1 + SpecialFunctions.erf(z / sqrt(2.0)))

    x1b1     = Zmat * fit.γ
    x2b2     = Xmat * fit.β
    probpos  = Φ_.(x1b1)
    sig2sq   = fit.σ^2
    sig12sq  = textbook_bug ? fit.ρ * fit.σ^2 : fit.ρ * fit.σ

    yhatheck    = exp.(x2b2 .+ 0.5 .* sig2sq) .*
                  (1 .- Φ_.(.-x1b1 .- sig12sq))
    yhatposheck = yhatheck ./ probpos

    return (; probpos, x1b1, x2b2,
              sig2sq, sig12sq, sigma1sq = 1.0,
              yhatheck, yhatposheck)
end

"""
    predict_tobit_lognormal_stata(fit; σ = fit.σ, γ::Real,
                                  X = fit.X, truncated::Bool = false)

Lognormal-tobit prediction of `y = exp(ln_y)` from a `tobit_stata` fit on
`ln(y)` left-censored at `γ`. With xβ = X β̂:

  yhat_i = exp(xβ_i + ½σ²) · (1 − Φ((γ − xβ_i − σ²)/σ))   (E[y | x])
  ytrunc_i = yhat_i / (1 − Φ((γ − xβ_i)/σ))               (E[y | x, y>0])

`σ` defaults to the fitted σ̂ but can be overridden — used in the textbook's
"poor predictions are due to high σ" sensitivity check (σ = 1, σ = 2 vs σ̂).
"""
function predict_tobit_lognormal_stata(fit; σ::Real = fit.σ, γ::Real,
                                       X::AbstractMatrix = fit.X,
                                       truncated::Bool = false)
    Φ_(z) = 0.5 * (1 + SpecialFunctions.erf(z / sqrt(2.0)))
    xb = X * fit.β
    yhat = exp.(xb .+ 0.5 * σ^2) .*
           (1 .- Φ_.((γ .- xb .- σ^2) ./ σ))
    truncated || return yhat
    return yhat ./ (1 .- Φ_.((γ .- xb) ./ σ))
end

"""
    probit_stata(df, formula; vce=:oim, level=0.95, quiet=false) -> NamedTuple

Stata-style `probit <depvar> <regs> [, vce(robust)]`. Fits a Binomial GLM
with `ProbitLink` and prints Stata's exact `probit` output:

  - Header: Number of obs / LR chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 / Log likelihood / Pseudo R²
    (NB: `LR chi2`, NOT `Wald chi2` — Stata uses 2·(ll − ll_null) for the
    overall fit statistic in `probit` even with `vce(robust)`.)
  - Coefficient table in Stata-display order (slopes first, _cons last).

Returns `(; model, β, se, V, X, coefnames, ll, ll_null, pseudo_r2, n, k,
          β_glm, V_glm, X_glm, coefnames_glm)` so downstream code (e.g.
Heckman two-step) can reuse the fitted probit linear index.
"""
function probit_stata(df, formula; vce::Symbol=:oim, level::Float64=0.95,
                      quiet::Bool=false)
    needed = StatsModels.termvars(formula)
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, needed])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end
    # Drop any rows with non-finite values (NaN/Inf in computed columns
    # like `linc = log(hhincome)` would crash GLM.jl's IRLS at the
    # `isfinite(dev)` assertion). `dropmissing` only handles `Missing`.
    keep = trues(DataFrames.nrow(dfc))
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        eltype(col) <: Real || continue
        for i in eachindex(col)
            keep[i] &= isfinite(col[i])
        end
    end
    dfc = dfc[keep, :]
    # Fit probit. Default IRLS sometimes fails its `isfinite(dev)` assertion
    # when the design matrix has wide-range columns (e.g. `age2`); in that
    # case we warm-start from a logit fit's β rescaled by ≈1/1.81 (the
    # asymptotic logit→probit coefficient ratio sqrt(π/3)).
    m = try
        GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.ProbitLink())
    catch err
        if err isa AssertionError && occursin("isfinite", string(err))
            m_logit = GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.LogitLink())
            β_init  = GLM.coef(m_logit) ./ 1.81
            GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.ProbitLink();
                    start = β_init)
        else
            rethrow(err)
        end
    end
    β  = GLM.coef(m); cn = GLM.coefnames(m)
    n  = Int(StatsBase.nobs(m)); k = length(β)
    yv = Float64.(GLM.response(m))
    Xm = GLM.modelmatrix(m)

    V = if vce == :robust
        # Robust sandwich for probit: V = A · meat · A · (n/(n-1)) with
        # A = OIM vcov and meat = Σ s_i s_iᵀ where the per-obs score is
        # s_i = ((y_i − μ_i) / [μ_i(1−μ_i)]) · φ(η_i) · x_i.
        η  = Xm * β                                 # linear index
        μ  = GLM.predict(m)
        ϕ  = Distributions.pdf.(Distributions.Normal(), η)
        u  = (yv .- μ) ./ (μ .* (1 .- μ)) .* ϕ
        s  = u .* Xm
        meat = s' * s
        A = Matrix(GLM.vcov(m))                     # OIM vcov is A⁻¹ already
        A * meat * A * (n / (n - 1))
    else
        Matrix(GLM.vcov(m))
    end
    se = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    z  = β ./ se
    p_z = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    ci_lo = β .- crit .* se
    ci_hi = β .+ crit .* se

    ll = GLM.loglikelihood(m)
    m_null = GLM.glm(StatsModels.term(Symbol(formula.lhs)) ~ StatsModels.term(1),
                     dfc, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.ProbitLink())
    ll_null = GLM.loglikelihood(m_null)
    pseudo_r2 = 1 - ll / ll_null
    LR = 2 * (ll - ll_null)
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx = setdiff(1:k, [intercept_idx])
    LR_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), LR)

    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    if !quiet
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %6s\n",
                       "Probit regression", "Number of obs", commafmt(n))
        Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.2f\n", "",
                       "LR chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", LR)
        Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.4f\n", "", "Prob > chi2", LR_p)
        ll_str = Printf.@sprintf("Log likelihood = %.4f", ll)
        r2_str = Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %6.4f", "Pseudo R2", pseudo_r2)
        pad    = max(0, 78 - length(ll_str) - length(r2_str))
        println(ll_str, " "^pad, r2_str)
        println()

        println("-"^78)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  Std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(formula.lhs), 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        ord = intercept_idx === nothing ? collect(slope_idx) :
                                          vcat(slope_idx, [intercept_idx])
        for i in ord
            label = cn[i] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : cn[i]
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           label, g9(β[i]; w=10), g9(se[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_z[i]),
                           g9(ci_lo[i]; w=9), g9(ci_hi[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^78)
    end

    intercept_idx2 = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx2     = setdiff(1:k, [intercept_idx2])
    ord2 = intercept_idx2 === nothing ? collect(slope_idx2) :
                                        vcat(slope_idx2, [intercept_idx2])
    cn_ord = intercept_idx2 === nothing ? cn[ord2] :
                                          vcat(cn[slope_idx2], "_cons")
    return (; model = m, β = β[ord2], se = se[ord2], V = V[ord2, ord2],
              X = Xm[:, ord2], coefnames = cn_ord,
              ll, ll_null, pseudo_r2, LR, LR_p, n, k,
              β_glm = β, V_glm = V, X_glm = Xm, coefnames_glm = cn)
end

"""
    ologit_probs(β, τ, X, J) -> Matrix{Float64}

Stata `predict, pr` after `ologit`. Returns an `N × J` matrix of
predicted P(y = j) for each row of `X`. With τ_0 = −∞, τ_J = +∞:

    P[i, 1] = Λ(τ_1 − xᵢ'β)
    P[i, j] = Λ(τ_j − xᵢ'β) − Λ(τ_{j−1} − xᵢ'β)    for 1 < j < J
    P[i, J] = 1 − Λ(τ_{J−1} − xᵢ'β)
"""
function tobit_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, depvar::Symbol,
                   regs::AbstractVector{Symbol};
                   ll::Union{Nothing,Real} = 0.0,
                   ul::Union{Nothing,Real} = nothing,
                   level::Float64 = 0.95,
                   quiet::Bool = false)
    cols = vcat([depvar], collect(regs))
    dfc  = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, cols])
    for c in cols
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing,Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(_rawval.(col))
        end
    end
    y = Float64.(_rawval.(dfc[!, depvar]))
    X = hcat([Float64.(_rawval.(dfc[!, r])) for r in regs]..., ones(length(y)))
    N, k = size(X)
    nparam = k + 1                              # β (k) + lnσ
    coefnames = [string.(regs)..., "_cons"]

    # Stable Φ / log-Φ using erf and erfcx for the tails.
    Φ_(x) = 0.5 * (1 + erf(x / sqrt(2.0)))
    φ_(x) = exp(-x^2 / 2) / sqrt(2 * Base.pi)

    function negll(θ)
        β = view(θ, 1:k); σ = exp(θ[end])
        η = X * β
        ll_acc = zero(eltype(θ))
        for i in 1:N
            yi = y[i]
            if ll !== nothing && yi <= ll
                # Left-censored: log P(y* ≤ ll) = log Φ((ll - η)/σ)
                z = (ll - η[i]) / σ
                ll_acc += log(max(Φ_(z), eps(Float64)))
            elseif ul !== nothing && yi >= ul
                # Right-censored: log Φ((η - ul)/σ) = log(1 - Φ((ul - η)/σ))
                z = (η[i] - ul) / σ
                ll_acc += log(max(Φ_(z), eps(Float64)))
            else
                # Uncensored: log[φ((y - η)/σ)/σ]
                z = (yi - η[i]) / σ
                ll_acc += -log(σ) - 0.5 * log(2 * Base.pi) - 0.5 * z^2
            end
        end
        return -ll_acc
    end

    # Warm start: OLS β on uncensored part (or full sample) + lnσ from
    # OLS residuals.
    function _ols_warm()
        mask = ll === nothing ? trues(N) : (y .> ll)
        if sum(mask) > k
            Xu = X[mask, :]; yu = y[mask]
            βu = Xu \ yu
            σu = Statistics.std(yu .- Xu * βu)
            return vcat(βu, log(max(σu, eps(Float64))))
        end
        return vcat(zeros(k), 0.0)
    end
    θ0 = _ols_warm()
    res = _optimize_compat(negll, θ0, Optim.LBFGS(),
                         Optim.Options(g_tol = 1e-8, iterations = 4000);
                         autodiff = :forward)
    θ̂  = Optim.minimizer(res)
    β̂  = θ̂[1:k]; σ̂ = exp(θ̂[end])
    llv = -negll(θ̂)

    function _fd_hessian(f, x)
        nθ = length(x); H = zeros(nθ, nθ)
        h_ = sqrt(sqrt(eps(Float64))) .* max.(abs.(x), 1.0); f0 = f(x)
        for i in 1:nθ
            xpi = copy(x); xmi = copy(x); xpi[i] += h_[i]; xmi[i] -= h_[i]
            H[i, i] = (f(xpi) - 2*f0 + f(xmi)) / h_[i]^2
            for j in (i+1):nθ
                xpp = copy(x); xpp[i] += h_[i]; xpp[j] += h_[j]
                xpm = copy(x); xpm[i] += h_[i]; xpm[j] -= h_[j]
                xmp = copy(x); xmp[i] -= h_[i]; xmp[j] += h_[j]
                xmm = copy(x); xmm[i] -= h_[i]; xmm[j] -= h_[j]
                H[i, j] = H[j, i] =
                    (f(xpp) - f(xpm) - f(xmp) + f(xmm)) / (4*h_[i]*h_[j])
            end
        end
        return H
    end
    V_raw = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(_fd_hessian(negll, θ̂)))
    # Delta-method on σ = exp(lnσ): dσ/dlnσ = σ.
    Jmat = Matrix{Float64}(LinearAlgebra.I, nparam, nparam)
    Jmat[end, end] = σ̂
    V = Jmat * V_raw * Jmat'
    se = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    se_β = se[1:k]; se_σ = se[end]

    n_left_cens  = ll === nothing ? 0 : sum(y .<= ll)
    n_right_cens = ul === nothing ? 0 : sum(y .>= ul)
    n_uncens     = N - n_left_cens - n_right_cens

    if !quiet
        function g9(x; w::Int = 10, sig::Int = 7)
            (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
            su = sig; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", su, x)
            cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
            while length(s) > cap && su > 1
                su -= 1; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", su, x)
            end
            0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
            lpad(s, w)
        end
        commafmt(num) = begin
            s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
            while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
            (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
        end
        crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(),
                                      1 - (1 - level) / 2)
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %6s\n", "Tobit regression",
                       "Number of obs", commafmt(N))
        Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6s\n", "",
                       "  Uncensored", commafmt(n_uncens))
        ll === nothing || Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6s\n", "",
                       "  Left-cens.", commafmt(n_left_cens))
        ul === nothing || Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6s\n", "",
                       "  Right-cens.", commafmt(n_right_cens))
        println(Printf.@sprintf("Log likelihood = %.4f\n", llv))

        println("-"^78)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  Std. err.      t    P>|t|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(depvar), 100 * level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        for c in 1:k
            label = c == k ? "_cons" : string(regs[c])
            b = β̂[c]; s = se_β[c]; z = b/s
            pp = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z)))
            lo = b - crit*s; hi = b + crit*s
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           label, g9(b; w=10), g9(s; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", pp),
                           g9(lo; w=9), g9(hi; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s\n", "/sigma",
                       g9(σ̂; w=10), g9(se_σ; w=9))
        println("-"^78)
    end

    return (; β = β̂, σ = σ̂, V, se_β, se_σ, ll = llv,
              X, regs = collect(regs), coefnames,
              n = N, n_uncens, n_left_cens, n_right_cens,
              nparam, ll_bound = ll, ul_bound = ul,
              depvar_name = depvar)
end

"""
    margins_tobit_stata(res; predict, at=:mean, level=0.95, quiet=false)
        -> NamedTuple

Stata `margins, dydx(*) predict(...)` after `tobit`. The `predict`
keyword selects which prediction to compute:

* `:xb`        — linear index xβ
* `:e_cond`    — E[y | L < y < U, x] (Stata `predict(e(L, U))`,
                 default L = lower-censoring point, U = ∞ if no
                 upper bound)
* `:e_uncond`  — censored expectation E[y* | x] where y* = max(L,
                 min(y, U)) (Stata `predict(ystar(L, U))`)
* `:pr`        — P(L < y < U | x) (Stata `predict(pr(L, U))`)

`at = :mean` (Stata's `atmean`, MEM) uses column means of `res.X`;
`at = :asobserved` (AME) averages per-observation ME. Bounds default
to `res.ll_bound` (lower) and `res.ul_bound` (upper); override with
`lower`/`upper` kwargs.

SE is delta-method on (β, σ) via a central-FD Jacobian of the mean
ME against `res.V`.
"""
function margins_tobit_stata(res; predict::Symbol = :e_cond,
                             at = :mean,
                             lower::Union{Nothing,Real} = nothing,
                             upper::Union{Nothing,Real} = nothing,
                             level::Float64 = 0.95,
                             quiet::Bool = false)
    L = lower === nothing ?
        (res.ll_bound === nothing ? -Inf : Float64(res.ll_bound)) :
        Float64(lower)
    U = upper === nothing ?
        (res.ul_bound === nothing ?  Inf : Float64(res.ul_bound)) :
        Float64(upper)

    X = res.X; k = size(X, 2)
    Xeval = at === :mean       ? reshape(vec(Statistics.mean(X; dims = 1)),
                                         1, k) :
            at === :asobserved ? X :
            reshape(convert(Vector{Float64}, at), 1, k)

    Φ_(z) = 0.5 * (1 + erf(z / sqrt(2.0)))
    φ_(z) = exp(-z^2 / 2) / sqrt(2 * Base.pi)

    # Analytical per-row marginal effect ∂(predicted)/∂x_c for each
    # `predict` type. Closed forms avoid the inner-FD numerical noise
    # of evaluating ∂pred/∂x_c by finite differences and let us
    # delta-method clean on θ via a single outer FD.
    function me_at(θ, c)
        β = view(θ, 1:k); σ = exp(θ[end])
        Nrows = size(Xeval, 1); acc = zero(eltype(θ))
        for i in 1:Nrows
            xi = view(Xeval, i, :)
            η  = LinearAlgebra.dot(xi, β)
            z  = η / σ
            βc = β[c]
            row_me = if predict === :xb
                βc
            elseif predict === :pr
                # ∂[Φ((U-η)/σ) − Φ((L-η)/σ)]/∂x_c = (β_c/σ)·[φ((L-η)/σ) − φ((U-η)/σ)]
                a_phi = isfinite(L) ? φ_((L - η)/σ) : zero(eltype(θ))
                b_phi = isfinite(U) ? φ_((U - η)/σ) : zero(eltype(θ))
                βc / σ * (a_phi - b_phi)
            elseif predict === :e_uncond
                # For ystar(L, U) the simple identity holds for one-sided
                # left censoring at L (Stata's typical use): ∂E[y*]/∂x_c
                # = β_c · [Φ((U-η)/σ) − Φ((L-η)/σ)]. For the two-sided
                # case the same probability-of-uncensored factor applies.
                Φa = isfinite(L) ? Φ_((L - η)/σ) : zero(eltype(θ))
                Φb = isfinite(U) ? Φ_((U - η)/σ) :  one(eltype(θ))
                βc * (Φb - Φa)
            elseif predict === :e_cond
                # ∂E[y | L<y<U] / ∂x_c = β_c · (Var[y|L<y<U] / σ²)
                # Var/σ² = 1 + α·φ(α)/D − β·φ(β)/D − ((φ(α)−φ(β))/D)²
                # where α = (L-η)/σ, β = (U-η)/σ, D = Φ(β) − Φ(α),
                #       λ_a = φ(α)/D, λ_b = φ(β)/D.
                a = isfinite(L) ? (L - η)/σ : -convert(eltype(θ), Inf)
                b = isfinite(U) ? (U - η)/σ :  convert(eltype(θ), Inf)
                Φa = isfinite(a) ? Φ_(a) : zero(eltype(θ))
                Φb = isfinite(b) ? Φ_(b) :  one(eltype(θ))
                φa = isfinite(a) ? φ_(a) : zero(eltype(θ))
                φb = isfinite(b) ? φ_(b) : zero(eltype(θ))
                denom = max(Φb - Φa, eps(Float64))
                λ_a = φa / denom
                λ_b = φb / denom
                a_term = isfinite(a) ? a * λ_a : zero(eltype(θ))
                b_term = isfinite(b) ? b * λ_b : zero(eltype(θ))
                βc * (1 - (λ_a - λ_b)^2 + a_term - b_term)
            else
                error("unknown predict type: $predict")
            end
            acc += row_me
        end
        return acc / Nrows
    end

    θ̂ = vcat(res.β, log(res.σ))
    # Use res.V which is in (β, σ) units — the residual delta-method
    # already converts lnσ → σ inside `tobit_stata`. But our `pred`
    # consumes (β, lnσ), so we need V in that parametrisation. Solve
    # via Jacobian inverse: V_raw = J⁻¹ · V · (J⁻¹)' with J = diag(1,
    # …, 1, σ).
    Jinv = Matrix{Float64}(LinearAlgebra.I, k + 1, k + 1)
    Jinv[end, end] = 1 / res.σ
    V_raw = Jinv * res.V * Jinv'

    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(),
                                  1 - (1 - level) / 2)
    h_step = sqrt(eps(Float64))
    rows = NamedTuple[]
    # Iterate slope coefficients (exclude the constant — coefnames[end]).
    for c in 1:(k - 1)
        m_pt = me_at(θ̂, c)
        g = zeros(length(θ̂))
        for i in eachindex(θ̂)
            step = max(abs(θ̂[i]) * h_step, h_step)
            tp = copy(θ̂); tp[i] += step
            tm = copy(θ̂); tm[i] -= step
            g[i] = (me_at(tp, c) - me_at(tm, c)) / (2 * step)
        end
        se = sqrt(max(g' * V_raw * g, 0.0))
        z  = m_pt / se
        p  = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z)))
        push!(rows, (; reg = Symbol(res.coefnames[c]),
                      dydx = m_pt, se, z, p,
                      ci_lo = m_pt - crit * se, ci_hi = m_pt + crit * se))
    end

    if !quiet
        function g9(x; w::Int = 10, sig::Int = 7)
            (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
            su = sig; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", su, x)
            cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
            while length(s) > cap && su > 1
                su -= 1; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", su, x)
            end
            0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
            lpad(s, w)
        end
        commafmt(num) = begin
            s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
            while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
            (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
        end
        N = size(X, 1)
        println()
        title = at === :asobserved ? "Average marginal effects" :
                                     "Conditional marginal effects"
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %6s\n", title,
                       "Number of obs", commafmt(N))
        println("Model VCE: OIM")
        expr_str = predict === :xb       ? "linear prediction xβ" :
                   predict === :e_cond   ? "E[y | $(L) < y < $(U)]" :
                   predict === :e_uncond ? "E[y* | x]  (censored at $(L), $(U))" :
                   predict === :pr       ? "P($(L) < y < $(U))" : "?"
        println("Expression: ", expr_str)
        println()
        println("-"^78)
        println("             |            Delta-method")
        Printf.@printf("%12s |      dy/dx   Std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       "", 100 * level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        for r in rows
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           string(r.reg),
                           g9(r.dydx; w = 10), g9(r.se; w = 9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", r.z),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", r.p),
                           g9(r.ci_lo; w = 9), g9(r.ci_hi; w = 10))
        end
        println("-"^78)
    end

    return (; rows, predict, at = Xeval, lower = L, upper = U, n = size(X, 1))
end

function ologit_probs(β, τ, X, J)
    n = size(X, 1)
    P = zeros(n, J)
    Λ(z) = 1 / (1 + exp(-z))
    for i in 1:n
        η = LinearAlgebra.dot(view(X, i, :), β)
        P[i, 1] = Λ(τ[1] - η)
        for j in 2:(J - 1)
            P[i, j] = Λ(τ[j] - η) - Λ(τ[j - 1] - η)
        end
        P[i, J] = 1 - Λ(τ[J - 1] - η)
    end
    return P
end

"""
    heckman_twostep_stata(df, fml_outcome, fml_selection;
                         depvar_y="lny", depvar_d="dy", level=0.95, quiet=false)

Stata-style `heckman <y> <xs>, select(<d> = <zs>) twostep`. Implements the
classic Heckman (1979) two-step estimator with proper variance correction
for the first-stage probit estimation:

  Stage 1: probit(`d ~ zs`) on full sample → γ̂
           λ_i = φ(z_i'γ̂)/Φ(z_i'γ̂)
  Stage 2: OLS(`y ~ xs + λ`) on positive subsample → α̂ = (β̂, β̂_λ)
           σ̂² = (ε̂'ε̂)/n₂ + β̂_λ² · mean(δ_i over positives)
                where δ_i = λ_i · (λ_i + z_i'γ̂)
           ρ̂ = β̂_λ / σ̂   (and Stata's `lambda` output is β̂_λ = ρ̂·σ̂)

The variance of α̂ corrects for stage-1 sampling variability:
  V(α̂) = σ̂² · (X*'X*)⁻¹ · {X*'(I − ρ̂²Δ)X* + ρ̂²·X*'Δ·Z·Vγ·Z'Δ·X*} · (X*'X*)⁻¹
  where X* = [X_pos | λ_pos], Δ = diag(δ_pos), Vγ = (Z'diag(δ_full)Z)⁻¹.

Prints Stata's three-block output (lny / dy / /mills) with the corrected SEs
plus σ̂ and ρ̂. Returns the NamedTuple
`(; β_outcome, β_selection, β_lambda, σ, ρ, V_outcome, n, n_pos, n_zero, …)`.
"""
function heckman_twostep_stata(df, fml_outcome, fml_selection;
                               depvar_y::AbstractString="lny",
                               depvar_d::AbstractString="dy",
                               level::Float64=0.95, quiet::Bool=false)
    # Stage 1 — probit on the FULL sample with non-missing SELECTION vars
    # only. We must NOT dropmissing on outcome vars here, since the outcome
    # variable (e.g. `lny`) is legitimately missing for unselected rows
    # (where y = 0). Including it in the dropmissing would eliminate the
    # unselected rows and make the probit degenerate (all dy = 1).
    sel_vars = StatsModels.termvars(fml_selection)
    out_vars = StatsModels.termvars(fml_outcome)
    needed   = unique(vcat(sel_vars, out_vars))
    # `dropmissing(df, cols)` only requires `cols` to be non-missing while
    # keeping all columns. Outcome `lny` retains its missing values.
    df_h = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, needed], sel_vars)
    n_full = DataFrames.nrow(df_h)

    m_pr = GLM.glm(fml_selection, df_h,
                   Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.ProbitLink())
    γ̂   = GLM.coef(m_pr); cn_pr = GLM.coefnames(m_pr)
    Z   = GLM.modelmatrix(m_pr)
    xb_full = Z * γ̂
    λ_full  = Distributions.pdf.(Distributions.Normal(), xb_full) ./
              Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), xb_full)
    δ_full  = λ_full .* (λ_full .+ xb_full)

    # Selection mask. Use plain `Int == 1` rather than `Float64 > 0` because
    # some loaded packages in some sessions type-pirate `>`/comparison
    # broadcasting for Float64. `Int == Int` is essentially impossible to
    # pirate, so this form is robust.
    d_full = Int.(df_h[!, Symbol(depvar_d)])
    is_pos = Bool[d == 1 for d in d_full]
    n_pos  = sum(is_pos); n_zero = n_full - n_pos

    # Stage 2 — OLS on positives, with λ as additional regressor
    df_pos = df_h[is_pos, :]
    df_pos.invmills = λ_full[is_pos]
    fml_ols = StatsModels.term(Symbol(depvar_y)) ~
              sum(StatsModels.term.(out_vars[2:end])) +
              StatsModels.term(:invmills)
    # Build X_pos manually so we control column order
    out_xs = out_vars[2:end]   # skip lhs
    X_pos  = hcat(ones(n_pos),
                 [Float64.(df_pos[!, v]) for v in out_xs]...,
                 df_pos.invmills)
    y_pos  = Float64.(df_pos[!, Symbol(depvar_y)])
    α̂      = X_pos \ y_pos
    ε̂      = y_pos .- X_pos * α̂

    β̂_λ    = α̂[end]
    δ_pos  = δ_full[is_pos]
    σ̂²     = (ε̂'ε̂) / n_pos + β̂_λ^2 * Statistics.mean(δ_pos)
    σ̂      = sqrt(σ̂²)
    ρ̂      = β̂_λ / σ̂

    # Heckman 2-step variance with stage-1 correction. Use the probit
    # Fisher information matrix V(γ̂) = (Σ w_i z_i z_i')⁻¹ with
    # w_i = φ_i² / [Φ_i (1−Φ_i)] — this is what Stata's `heckman` uses for
    # the first-stage VCE, NOT the Heckman-1979 (Z'ΔZ)⁻¹ form (which gives
    # SEs ~0.2% larger because Δ ≠ Fisher info weights).
    safe_sym_inv(A; rtol::Float64=1e-10) = begin
        As = LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(A)
        try
            LinearAlgebra.inv(As)
        catch
            LinearAlgebra.pinv(Matrix(As); rtol=rtol)
        end
    end

    XX_inv = safe_sym_inv(X_pos' * X_pos)
    Φ_full = clamp.(Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), xb_full), 1e-12, 1 - 1e-12)
    φ_full = Distributions.pdf.(Distributions.Normal(), xb_full)
    w_full = (φ_full .^ 2) ./ (Φ_full .* (1 .- Φ_full))
    A_γ    = Z' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(w_full) * Z       # probit Fisher info
    Vγ     = safe_sym_inv(A_γ)
    Z_pos  = Z[is_pos, :]
    D_pos  = LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(δ_pos)
    M1     = X_pos' * (LinearAlgebra.I(n_pos) - ρ̂^2 .* D_pos) * X_pos
    M2     = ρ̂^2 .* (X_pos' * D_pos * Z_pos) * Vγ * (Z_pos' * D_pos * X_pos)
    V_α    = σ̂² .* XX_inv * (M1 + M2) * XX_inv
    se_α   = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V_α), 0.0))

    # Coefficient names for outcome (cons last, as Stata)
    cn_out = vcat(string.(out_xs), ["_cons"])
    # α̂ order: (Intercept), out_xs..., invmills. Reorder for Stata: out_xs, _cons.
    # Indices in α̂: 1=cons, 2..k+1=xs, k+2=invmills
    k_out  = length(out_xs)
    α̂_disp = vcat(α̂[2:k_out+1], [α̂[1]])
    se_disp = vcat(se_α[2:k_out+1], [se_α[1]])
    α_lam  = α̂[end]; se_lam = se_α[end]

    z_disp = α̂_disp ./ se_disp
    p_disp = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z_disp)))
    crit   = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    lo_disp = α̂_disp .- crit .* se_disp
    hi_disp = α̂_disp .+ crit .* se_disp

    z_lam = α_lam / se_lam
    p_lam = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z_lam)))
    lo_lam = α_lam - crit * se_lam; hi_lam = α_lam + crit * se_lam

    # Selection equation SEs from probit (no correction needed)
    se_pr = sqrt.(LinearAlgebra.diag(Matrix(GLM.vcov(m_pr))))
    z_pr  = γ̂ ./ se_pr
    p_pr  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z_pr)))
    lo_pr = γ̂ .- crit .* se_pr; hi_pr = γ̂ .+ crit .* se_pr
    i_int_pr = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn_pr)
    slope_pr = setdiff(1:length(γ̂), [i_int_pr])
    ord_pr   = vcat(slope_pr, [i_int_pr])
    cn_pr_ord = vcat(cn_pr[slope_pr], "_cons")
    γ̂_disp = γ̂[ord_pr]; se_pr_disp = se_pr[ord_pr]
    z_pr_disp = z_pr[ord_pr]; p_pr_disp = p_pr[ord_pr]
    lo_pr_disp = lo_pr[ord_pr]; hi_pr_disp = hi_pr[ord_pr]

    # Wald chi²(k_out) on outcome slopes — uses corrected V
    βs = α̂_disp[1:end-1]   # (without _cons)
    Vs = V_α[2:k_out+1, 2:k_out+1]
    Wald = try
        (βs' * (LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(Vs) \ βs))::Float64
    catch
        (βs' * LinearAlgebra.pinv(Vs) * βs)::Float64
    end
    Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(k_out), Wald)

    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    if !quiet
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%-48s%-13s = %10s\n",
                       "Heckman selection model -- two-step estimates",
                       "Number of obs", commafmt(n_full))
        Printf.@printf("%-48s    %-13s = %10s\n",
                       "(regression model with sample selection)",
                       "Selected", commafmt(n_pos))
        Printf.@printf("%-48s    %-13s = %10s\n",
                       "", "Nonselected", commafmt(n_zero))
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%48s%-13s = %10.2f\n", "",
                       "Wald chi2($(k_out))", Wald)
        Printf.@printf("%48s%-13s = %10.4f\n", "", "Prob > chi2", Wald_p)
        println()

        println("-"^78)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  Std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       "", 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

        # lny block
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", depvar_y)
        for i in 1:k_out
            label = string(out_xs[i])
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           label, g9(α̂_disp[i]; w=10), g9(se_disp[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_disp[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_disp[i]),
                           g9(lo_disp[i]; w=9), g9(hi_disp[i]; w=10))
        end
        # _cons row for outcome
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                       "_cons", g9(α̂_disp[end]; w=10), g9(se_disp[end]; w=9),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_disp[end]),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_disp[end]),
                       g9(lo_disp[end]; w=9), g9(hi_disp[end]; w=10))
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

        # dy block
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", depvar_d)
        for i in eachindex(γ̂_disp)
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           cn_pr_ord[i],
                           g9(γ̂_disp[i]; w=10), g9(se_pr_disp[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_pr_disp[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_pr_disp[i]),
                           g9(lo_pr_disp[i]; w=9), g9(hi_pr_disp[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

        # /mills block
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", "/mills")
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                       "lambda",
                       g9(α_lam; w=10), g9(se_lam; w=9),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_lam),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_lam),
                       g9(lo_lam; w=9), g9(hi_lam; w=10))
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s\n", "rho",   Printf.@sprintf("%9.5f",  ρ̂))
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s\n", "sigma", Printf.@sprintf("%9.7f", σ̂))
        println("-"^78)
    end

    α̂_outcome_dict = Dict(zip(vcat(string.(out_xs), ["_cons"]), α̂_disp))
    return (; β_outcome = α̂_disp, se_outcome = se_disp, V_outcome = V_α,
              β_selection = γ̂, se_selection = se_pr, β_lambda = α_lam,
              se_lambda = se_lam, σ = σ̂, ρ = ρ̂,
              n = n_full, n_pos, n_zero,
              outcome_coefnames = vcat(string.(out_xs), ["_cons"]),
              selection_coefnames = cn_pr_ord)
end
```

### 16.3.1 Data summary

The data come from Deb, Munkin and Trivedi (2006), "Bayesian Analysis of
Two-Part Model with Endogeneity", *Journal of Applied Econometrics*. The
dependent variable `ambexp` is ambulatory medical expenditure (in dollars),
left-censored at zero. Regressors include insurance type, chronic diseases,
age, sex, education and ethnicity.

```{julia}
#=

* "Bayesian Analysis of Two-Part Model with Endogeneity", Journal of Applied Econometrics, 21, 1081-1100
* Only the data for year 2001 are used

* Dependent variable is 
*      ambexp   Ambulatory medical expenditures (excluding dental and outpatient mental) 
*      lambexp  Ln(ambexp) given ambexp > 0 ; missing otherwise

*       totchr     number of chronic diseases
*  - Socioeconomic characteristics
*       age     age in years/10 
*       female   1 for females, zero otherwise
*       educ     years of schooling of decision maker
*       blhisp   either black or hispanic
=#
```

### 16.3.2 Tobit analysis

```{julia}
#=
* Tobit analysis for ambexp using all expenditures
global xlist age female educ blhisp totchr ins   //Define regressor list $xlist
tobit ambexp $xlist, ll(0) 
=#
#=
* Tobit analysis for ambexp using all expenditures
global xlist age female educ blhisp totchr ins   //Define regressor list $xlist
tobit ambexp $xlist, ll(0)
=#

# `tobit_stata` (chunk 1) fits a Tobit MLE with left-censoring at 0
# (Stata's `ll(0)`) by LBFGS + autodiff gradient; OIM vcov via FD
# Hessian with delta-method on σ = exp(lnσ). The returned NamedTuple
# binds `β`, `σ`, `X`, `coefnames` so the downstream §16.3.3 / .4
# prediction / marginal-effect chunks can read `β_tob`, `σ_tob`,
# `X16`, `xnms16` directly.
tobit_res = tobit_stata(df16, :ambexp,
    [:age, :female, :educ, :blhisp, :totchr, :ins]; ll = 0.0)
β_tob   = tobit_res.β
σ_tob   = tobit_res.σ
X16     = tobit_res.X
xnms16  = tobit_res.coefnames;
```

### 16.3.3 Prediction after tobit

```{julia}
#=
* Tobit prediction and summary
predict yhatlin 
summarize yhatlin
=#
#=
* Tobit prediction and summary
predict yhatlin
summarize yhatlin
=#

# Stata's bare `predict <name>` after `tobit` returns the linear
# prediction xβ (the latent index — *no* censoring adjustment). We
# compute it as `X16 * β_tob` and feed it to `summarize_stata`
# (chunk 1) wrapped in a single-column DataFrame.
yhatlin = X16 * β_tob
summarize_stata(DataFrames.DataFrame(yhatlin = yhatlin), [:yhatlin]);
```

### 16.3.4 Marginal effects

#### Censored / uncensored / truncated expectations

```{julia}
#=
** Tobit postestimation

* (1) ME on censored expected value E(y|x,y>0)
quietly tobit ambexp age i.female educ i.blhisp totchr i.ins, ll(0)
margins, dydx(*) predict(e(0,.)) atmean noatlegend
=#

# `margins_tobit_stata` (chunk 1) — Stata's `margins, dydx(*)
# predict(e(0, .)) atmean noatlegend` after `tobit`. `predict =
# :e_cond` selects the truncated conditional expectation
# `E[y | L < y < U, x]` with `L`/`U` defaulting to the censoring
# bounds from the fit (here `lower = 0`, `upper = ∞`). At-mean
# evaluation matches Stata's `atmean`; SE is delta-method.
margins_tobit_stata(tobit_res; predict = :e_cond, at = :mean);
```

```{julia}
#=
* (2) ME without censoring on E(y|x)
margins, dydx(*) predict(ystar(0,.)) atmean noatlegend
=#

# `margins_tobit_stata` (chunk 1) — Stata's `margins, dydx(*)
# predict(ystar(0, .)) atmean` after `tobit`. `predict = :e_uncond`
# is the censored unconditional expectation `E[y* | x]` where
# `y* = max(L, min(y, U))`. Defaults to the fit's censoring bounds
# (`lower = 0`, `upper = ∞` here); SE is delta-method.
margins_tobit_stata(tobit_res; predict = :e_uncond, at = :mean);
```

```{julia}
#=
* (3) ME when E(y|0<y<535)
margins, dydx(*) predict(e(0,535)) atmean noatlegend
=#

# Same `margins_tobit_stata` (chunk 1), now with `upper = 535` for
# the doubly-truncated conditional expectation `E[y | 0 < y < 535]`.
# The helper's closed-form ME formula picks up the two-sided
# truncation term automatically; SE is delta-method.
margins_tobit_stata(tobit_res; predict = :e_cond, at = :mean,
                    lower = 0.0, upper = 535.0);
```

#### Left-censored case computed directly

```{julia}
#=
* Direct computation of marginal effects for E(y|x)
predict xb1, xb // xb1 is estimate of x'b
matrix btobit = e(b)
scalar sigma = btobit[1,11] // sigma is estimate of sigma
matrix bcoeff = btobit[1,1..9] // bcoeff is betas excl. constant
quietly summarize xb1 
scalar meanxb = r(mean) // mean of x'b equals (mean of x)'b 
scalar PHI = normal(meanxb/sigma) 
matrix deriv = PHI*bcoeff 
matrix list deriv 
=#
#=
* Direct computation of marginal effects for E(y|x)
predict xb1, xb // xb1 is estimate of x'b
matrix btobit = e(b)
scalar sigma = btobit[1,11] // sigma is estimate of sigma
matrix bcoeff = btobit[1,1..9] // bcoeff is betas excl. constant
quietly summarize xb1
scalar meanxb = r(mean) // mean of x'b equals (mean of x)'b
scalar PHI = normal(meanxb/sigma)
matrix deriv = PHI*bcoeff
matrix list deriv
=#

# Direct closed-form ∂E[y|x]/∂x_j = Φ(meanxb/σ) · β_j, in the explicit
# element-by-element form Stata's `matrix list deriv` shows. This
# produces the same numbers as `margins_tobit_stata(...; predict =
# :e_uncond, at = :mean)` — they're two ways to compute the same
# closed-form ME.
#
# Heads-up: Stata's pasted `deriv` from the postestimation block
# shows values that are ≈ 0.757 × the math-correct ones (and ≈
# 0.5 × β, implying Φ ≈ 0.5 ⇒ meanxb ≈ 0). That doesn't match the
# textbook formula or `margins, predict(ystar(0,.)) atmean` output —
# we suspect Stata's `predict xb1, xb` after the factor-variable
# refit is returning something other than X'β + _cons. The values
# below are the mathematically-correct closed-form derivatives;
# they match Stata's own `margins, predict(ystar(0,.)) atmean`.
xb1     = X16 * β_tob
meanxb  = Statistics.mean(xb1)
PHI     = 0.5 * (1 + SpecialFunctions.erf((meanxb / σ_tob) / sqrt(2.0)))
deriv   = PHI .* β_tob[1:end - 1]
Printf.@printf("\nmeanxb = %.4f   σ = %.4f   Φ(meanxb/σ) = %.6f\n\n",
               meanxb, σ_tob, PHI)
println("deriv[1, 1..$(length(deriv))]:")
for (n, d) in zip(xnms16[1:end - 1], deriv)
    Printf.@printf("%-10s  %12.6f\n", n, d)
end
```

```{julia}
#=
* The following gives nicer looking results
ereturn post deriv 
ereturn display
=#
#=
* The following gives nicer looking results
ereturn post deriv
ereturn display
=#

# Stata's `ereturn post deriv; ereturn display` reposts `deriv` as
# e(b) and prints it through the standard coefficient-table renderer
# (no SE since `deriv` is a bare vector). We mimic the layout with
# a one-column variable / Coefficient table.
println()
println("-"^60)
Printf.@printf("%12s | %12s\n", "", "Coefficient")
println("-"^13, "+", "-"^46)
for (n, d) in zip(xnms16[1:end - 1], deriv)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %12.6f\n", n, d)
end
println("-"^60)
```

#### Marginal impact on probabilities

```{julia}
#=
* Compute margins on Pr(5000<ambexp<10000)  
quietly tobit ambexp age i.female educ i.blhisp totchr i.ins, ll(0) vce(robust)
margins, dydx(*) predict(pr(5000,10000)) atmean noatlegend
=#
#=
* Compute margins on Pr(5000<ambexp<10000)
quietly tobit ambexp age i.female educ i.blhisp totchr i.ins, ll(0) vce(robust)
margins, dydx(*) predict(pr(5000,10000)) atmean noatlegend
=#

# Same `margins_tobit_stata` (chunk 1) helper, with `predict = :pr`
# and the doubly-truncated probability interval `(5000, 10000)`.
# Stata's closed-form ∂P(L < y < U)/∂x_c = (β_c/σ)·[φ((L-η)/σ) −
# φ((U-η)/σ)] is what the helper's `:pr` branch evaluates. The
# Stata refit with `vce(robust)` would use sandwich SEs; our helper
# reports OIM SEs.
margins_tobit_stata(tobit_res; predict = :pr, at = :mean,
                    lower = 5000.0, upper = 10000.0);
```

## 16.4 Tobit for lognormal data

### 16.4.1 Data example

The dependent variable `lny` is `ln(ambexp)` if positive, with the censored
zeros mapped to a small value `γ - ε` to keep them on the same scale.

```{julia}
#=
* ASIDE: IN BELOW ....
* We observe  y = 0       if dy=0   and  y = y  if dy=1
* Let gamma be the smallest of the positive y's
* We define lny = gamma-0.000001 if dy=0   and lny = ln(y) if dy=1 
* This ensures that tobit, ll will correctly sort out
* the censored and uncensored observations
* Note that can't set lny = 0 if dy=1 as ln(y) < 0 if gamma
* drop xb

* Summary of log(expenditures) for positives only
summarize lambexp, detail
=#
#=
* ASIDE: IN BELOW ....
* We observe  y = 0       if dy=0   and  y = y  if dy=1
* Let gamma be the smallest of the positive y's
* We define lny = gamma-0.000001 if dy=0   and lny = ln(y) if dy=1
* This ensures that tobit, ll will correctly sort out
* the censored and uncensored observations
* Note that can't set lny = 0 if dy=1 as ln(y) < 0 if gamma
* drop xb

* Summary of log(expenditures) for positives only
summarize lambexp, detail
=#

# `lambexp` is pre-computed in `mus16data.dta` as ln(ambexp) for
# positive expenditures (missing for ambexp == 0), so we just filter
# out the missings and feed it to `summarize_stata` (chunk 1) with
# `detail = true` for the Stata percentile / Smallest / Largest /
# moments block.
summarize_stata(DataFrames.dropmissing(df16, :lambexp),
                [:lambexp]; detail = true);
```

### 16.4.2 Setting the censoring point for the log model

```{julia}
#=
* "Tricking" Stata to handle log transformation
generate y = ambexp
generate dy = ambexp > 0
generate lny = ln(y)                // Zero values will become missing
quietly summarize lny
scalar gamma = r(min)               // This could be negative
display "gamma = " gamma
replace lny = gamma - 0.0000001 if lny == .
tabulate y if y < 0.02              // .02 is arbitrary small value
tabulate lny if lny < gamma + 0.02
* Label the variables
label variable y "ambexp"
label variable lny "lnambexp"
label variable dy "dambexp"
=#

# Recipe to map log-of-positives onto a tobit-friendly censored
# variable: zeros get a value just below the smallest log(positive)
# (`γ - 1e-7`), so a left-censored tobit at `γ` recovers the
# zero/positive split correctly.
df16.y   = Float64.(_rawval.(df16.ambexp))
df16.dy  = Int.(df16.y .> 0)
df16.lny = [yi > 0 ? log(yi) : missing for yi in df16.y]
γ_amb    = minimum(skipmissing(df16.lny))
Printf.@printf("gamma = %.10f\n", γ_amb)
df16.lny = [ismissing(v) ? γ_amb - 1e-7 : v for v in df16.lny]

# `tabulate y if y < 0.02` — frequency of y values near zero. With
# y the raw ambexp (continuous), this collapses to a count of
# y == 0 (the censored obs), since the next-smallest value of ambexp
# is well above 0.02.
tabulate_stata(DataFrames.filter(:y => <(0.02), df16), :y)
# `tabulate lny if lny < gamma + 0.02` — similar near-bound check on
# the log scale: should show the imputed `γ − 1e-7` value with a
# count equal to the number of zero-expenditure obs.
tabulate_stata(DataFrames.filter(:lny => <(γ_amb + 0.02), df16), :lny);
```

```{julia}
#=
// Not included in book
summarize y lny dy $xlist
summarize y lny dy, detail
=#

# `summarize_stata` (chunk 1) — first the basic block over y, lny,
# dy + the xlist (`$xlist = age female educ blhisp totchr ins`),
# then the Stata `, detail` percentile / Smallest / Largest /
# moments block for each of y, lny, dy (one section per variable).
summarize_stata(df16, [:y, :lny, :dy,
                       :age, :female, :educ, :blhisp, :totchr, :ins])
summarize_stata(df16, [:y, :lny, :dy]; detail = true);
```
